verses.gurmukhi: ਪਥਰੁ ਮੂਲਿ ਨ ਭਿਜਈ ਸਉ ਵਰੑਹਿਆਂ ਜਲਿ ਅੰਦਰਿ ਵਸੈ।
verses.translit_en: pathar mool na bhijiee sau var(h)hiaa(n) jal a(n)dhar vasai|

en.bdb: Even after remaining in water for a hundred years the stone would not get wet at all.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਥਰ ਖੇਤ ਨ ਜੰਮਈ ਚਾਰਿ ਮਹੀਨੇ ਇੰਦਰ ਵਰਸੈ।
verses.translit_en: pathar khet na ja(n)miee chaar maheene i(n)dhar varasai|

en.bdb: It may rain for four months continuously, but a stone would not sprout in the field.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਥਰਿ ਚੰਨਣੁ ਰਗੜੀਏ ਚੰਨਣ ਵਾਂਗਿ ਨ ਪਥਰੁ ਘਸੈ।
verses.translit_en: pathar cha(n)nan ragaRe'e cha(n)nan vaa(n)g na pathar ghasai|

en.bdb: A stone grinding sandal, never gets worn off like sandal.

verses.gurmukhi: ਸਿਲ ਵਟੇ ਨਿਤ ਪੀਸਦੇ ਰਸ ਕਸ ਜਾਣੈ ਵਾਸੁ ਨ ਰਸੈ।
verses.translit_en: sil vaTe nit peesadhe ras kas jaanai vaas na rasai|

en.bdb: Grinding stones always grind the material but never know about the taste and virtues of the things ground.

verses.gurmukhi: ਚਕੀ ਫਿਰੈ ਸਹੰਸਵਾਰ ਖਾਇ ਨ ਪੀਐ ਭੁਖ ਨ ਤਸੈ।
verses.translit_en: chakee firai saha(n)savaar khai na peeaai bhukh na tasai|

en.bdb: The grinding stone moves around thousands of times but it never feels hunger or thirst.

verses.gurmukhi: ਪਥਰ ਘੜੈ ਵਰਤਣਾ ਹੇਠਿ ਉਤੇ ਹੋਇ ਘੜਾ ਵਿਣਸੈ।
verses.translit_en: pathar ghaRai varatanaa heTh ute hoi ghaRaa vinasai|

en.bdb: The relationship between the stone and the pitcher is such that pitcher has to perish whether the stone strikes the pitcher or vice versa.
The stupid does not understand the difference between fame and infamy.
